record_notes.DCP-LETT-1666: April 11 with supplied 1855 year. Public request about whether seawater seed experiments were already attempted and most vulnerable kinds. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1684: Dated May 21, 1855; later self-reference calls it May 26 by publication, not different composition. Complete six-block article read including all twenty-three numbered seed types, cold/ordinary conditions, timings, small samples and survival limits. Earlier seed selection haphazard, new Hooker-selected set distinct. Challenges unsupported Forbes land bridges and poses centres-of-creation problem, not proof that every current distribution has one demonstrated mechanism. Rates from Johnston ten currents average thirty-three nautical miles/day; hypothetical 42-day transport, not witnessed ocean crossing. All tested loose seeds sink; whole plants/fruit floated is an assumption later corrected. Editorially reported clipping revisions (men/man, little above 32, survival wording, likelihood, solitary no) are undated later alterations, not silently substituted into May printed text. Oracle misspelling retained separately from orache identification. P1 acknowledges favourable editorial notice, not verbatim self-quotation or a surviving incoming letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1686A: Public request before May 26, 1855 with open lower XML fallback. Seeks Lacerta agilis eggs for planned floating/vitality tests; reward and postage promises are not completed collections. Earlier May 23 Fox letter intends this request, but no exact writing day can be deduced from publication bound. Down/Downe spelling as printed not silently regularised. No incoming prompt or demonstrated outcome.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1723: Public bee/nectar account before July 21, 1855; open XML lower bound not genuine composition year. Apparatus identifies observations in June 1843, June 26 1855 and July 12 1855; body has overcast twelfth then afternoon sunshine but no independently exact writing day. Observed hive bees at stipular glands differ from humble bees visiting flowers. Argues against nectar exclusively evolved for floral fertilisation while explicitly accepting insects often assist fertilisation; do not turn it into a denial of pollination. Gärtner selected-page discussion is demonstrated, not evidence entire work read this day. Names and modern interpretation remain distinct.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1771: Public questions before November 3, 1855 prompted by October 27 published shell-shower report, supporting a conditional post-publication window rather than XML 1809 start. Darwin misreads author as C. of Winchester; editor later identifies Charles Winchester at Osborne and Baird as conchologist. Keep his mistaken form in historical body. Asks whether shells living, area, duration, date, kinds and expert authentication; does not endorse a verified rain of shells. Later November 10 answer, Bree dispute and December apologies are future public voices in apparatus, not text Darwin already knows. Original incoming report not fully preserved as an independent source record.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1780: November 13 with supplied 1855 year. Complete long printed report of charlock emergence, recollected field history, dug plots and tagged seedlings. Darwin qualifies memory and improbability of new seed input; conclusion eight/nine-year survival is his inference, not controlled proof eliminating all dispersal. Preserve all reported patch/seed counts without arithmetic repair. Hooker warning about recent dispersed seeds is reported; no exact underlying note identified. Printed six plants is a misprint corrected in November 21 postscript to six plots of ground; preserve successive versions. November 10 editorial/Bentham material and earlier Kemp paper are referenced as context, not preserved direct prompt text. Darwin drafting Kemp article in older period does not make all quoted Kemp observations his own.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1783: November 21 with supplied 1855 year. Complete long article including own results and appended postscript. Germination timing is species/variety-specific, differing fresh/old seed and uncertain denominators preserved; 30/56 Capsicum is one measured count, not a universal percentage. Admits prior May assumption that ripe plants float was untested, now reports most sink within fourteen days and all except printed evergreens within a month. Future correction identifies Euonymus, not blanket evergreen survival. Conclusion limited to his dispersal experiments, no global refutation of ocean transport. Norwegian seeds separately tested and float; earlier Crowe/Hooker knowledge remains separate. Hooker points to Linnæus sentence; Darwin asks meaning instead of adopting an unverified seabed mechanism. P.S. corrects November 13 plants/plots misprint; postscript resides within same extracted P1 and must retain boundary and quote offsets.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1787: Public correction before December 1, 1855. Own last-week communication explicitly identifies printed evergreens as error for Euonymus; same-author textual correction, not an inbound/outgoing conversation pair. Correspondence supports later-than-November-21 composition without selecting exact day. Distinguishes dry longevity from saltwater or damp-soil survival; Solanaceae/Leguminosae comparison, fresh clover/bean retesting and possible plain-water harm qualified. Do not silently overwrite earlier printed 1783 version with later correction. Raw lower 1809 retained as metadata artifact.

November editorial prompt contextual, not fully preserved incoming communication. Exact composition day remains unknown.
